arguments.title: Historical note — Mosaic Commerce live ramp evidence
arguments.body: On October 6, 2025, Wes independently operated the scheduled Mosaic Commerce production-ramp watch as live traffic reached 16.0 million data points per minute, while Alex monitored cross-service invariants. Queue-wait p99 peaked at 286 ms and retryable queue-full responses at 0.11%; no numeric stop threshold persisted for five minutes, no tenant exceeded 64 pending batches, and consistency, dropped-series, shard-keeper lease, rollup-service parity, and full-health checks remained at baseline. No production change or rollback occurred, and the tenant-bounded control stayed enabled. The record explicitly noted that it measured accepted points—not accepted batches—so it did not establish whether an accepted batch was lost. This bounded live-ramp result was retained as formal evidence for Wes’s December 5, 2025 metrics-router ownership review; it did not, by itself, resolve the broader Mosaic scale-response cycle.
